g.text: FIGURE 3: EXACT DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS & INTEGRATING FACTORS TAXONOMY ENGINE
Euler-Schwarz Exactness Criterion, The 5 Integrating Factor Rules & Orthogonal Trajectories in Cartesian and Polar Systems
GATE 2027 TITANS ENGINE
SPEC: ULTRA-HD 4K BLUEPRINT
1. EXACTNESS TEST & INTEGRATION LAW
CANONICAL PFAFFIAN FORM: M(x, y) dx + N(x, y) dy = 0
Necessary and sufficient condition for exactness (Euler-Schwarz Theorem):
∂M / ∂y = ∂N / ∂x (M_y = N_x)
Physical meaning: The 2D differential form is the total differential of a scalar potential: dF = M dx + N dy = 0.
EXACT SOLUTION INTEGRATION LAW
∫ [y = const] M dx + ∫ [terms in N free from x] dy = C
(Integrate M w.r.t. x treating y as constant; integrate only pure-y terms of N w.r.t. y!)
⚠️ CRITICAL EXAM TRAP:
Do NOT integrate terms in N containing both x and y (e.g. 2xy, x²e^y); they are ALREADY accounted for in ∫ M dx!
INSTANT TOTAL DIFFERENTIAL IDENTITIES (INSPECTION)
• x dy + y dx = d(xy)
• (x dy - y dx) / x² = d(y/x) | (y dx - x dy) / y² = d(x/y)
• (x dy - y dx) / (xy) = d(ln(y/x)) | (x dy - y dx) / (x² + y²) = d(arctan(y/x))
• (x dx + y dy) / (x² + y²) = d(1/2 ln(x² + y²))
2. THE 5 INTEGRATING FACTOR RULES
RULE 1: HOMOGENEOUS M dx + N dy = 0
If M and N are homogeneous of the same degree and Mx + Ny ≠ 0:
IF = 1 / (Mx + Ny)
RULE 2: EQUATION OF THE FORM f₁(xy) y dx + f₂(xy) x dy = 0
If equation has xy product grouping and Mx - Ny ≠ 0:
IF = 1 / (Mx - Ny)
RULE 3: (1/N)(∂M/∂y - ∂N/∂x) = f(x) ALONE
If difference divided by N depends purely on independent variable x:
IF = e^(∫ f(x) dx) where f(x) = (1/N)(M_y - N_x)
Quick heuristic: Try this first when N is a single monomial or simpler than M.
RULE 4: (1/M)(∂N/∂x - ∂M/∂y) = g(y) ALONE
If reversed difference divided by M depends purely on variable y:
IF = e^(∫ g(y) dy) where g(y) = (1/M)(N_x - M_y)
⚠️ Notice sign swap: N_x - M_y (NOT M_y - N_x, else negative sign is missed!).
3. ORTHOGONAL TRAJECTORIES (CARTESIAN & POLAR)
A. CARTESIAN TRAJECTORY PIPELINE
Given family of curves F(x, y, c) = 0:
Step 1: Differentiate w.r.t. x and eliminate parameter c ⟹ f(x, y, dy/dx) = 0.
Step 2: Replace dy/dx with -dx/dy (Negative Reciprocal Slope):
dy/dx ⟶ - 1 / (dy/dx) = - dx/dy
Step 3: Solve the new differential equation.
Example: Parabolas y² = 4ax ⟹ 2y y' = 4a ⟹ y' = 2x/y ⟶ replace y' with -1/y' ⟹ Ellipses 2x² + y² = C!
B. POLAR TRAJECTORY PIPELINE
Given family of curves F(r, θ, c) = 0:
Step 1: Differentiate w.r.t. θ and eliminate parameter c ⟹ f(r, θ, dr/dθ) = 0.
Step 2: Replace dr/dθ with -r² (dθ/dr):
dr / dθ ⟶ - r² (dθ / dr)
Self-Orthogonal Family Property:
If replacing derivative leaves the ODE invariant, family is Self-Orthogonal (e.g. Confocal Parabolas y² = 4a(x + a)).
4. BENCHMARK CLASSROOM EXACT DRILL & INTEGRATING FACTOR RULE 3 VERIFICATION
PROBLEM FORMULATION
Solve the differential equation:
(2x cos y + 3x² y) dx + (x³ - x² sin y - y) dy = 0
STEP 1: IDENTIFY M & N
• M(x, y) = 2x cos y + 3x² y
• N(x, y) = x³ - x² sin y - y
STEP 2: PARTIAL DERIVATIVE TEST
∂M/∂y = -2x sin y + 3x²
∂N/∂x = 3x² - 2x sin y
VERDICT: ∂M/∂y ≡ ∂N/∂x ⟹ STRICTLY EXACT!
STEP 3: INTEGRATE M w.r.t. x (y CONSTANT)
∫ (2x cos y + 3x² y) dx = (cos y) x² + y x³ = x² cos y + x³ y
STEP 4: INTEGRATE TERMS IN N FREE FROM x
Terms in N without x: ONLY -y! ⟹ ∫ (-y) dy = - y² / 2
FINAL SOLUTION & VERIFICATION
EXACT SOLUTION RESULT:
x² cos y + x³ y - 1/2 y² = C
TOTAL DIFFERENTIAL VERIFICATION (CHECK BACK):
Let F(x, y) = x² cos y + x³ y - 1/2 y².
• F_x = ∂F/∂x = 2x cos y + 3x² y = M(x, y) ✓
• F_y = ∂F/∂y = -x² sin y + x³ - y = N(x, y) ✓
Why students lose marks on this problem in GATE:
1. Integrating x³ or -x² sin y in N again (causes double counting of x³y and x²cos y!).
2. Forgetting that cos y is treated as a CONSTANT during the x-integration.
3. Golden Rule: "Pure x gets M, pure y gets N, mixed terms get M only!"
SPEED: Solvable in < 45 seconds using exact formula!
NON-EXACT IF DRILL (RULE 3)
EQUATION: (x² + y² + 2x) dx + 2y dy = 0
1. M = x² + y² + 2x ⟹ M_y = 2y
2. N = 2y ⟹ N_x = 0 ⟹ M_y ≠ N_x (NOT EXACT!)
3. Test Rule 3:
4. Compute Integrating Factor:
IF = e^(∫ 1 dx) = e^x
5. Multiply equation by e^x:
e^x (x² + y² + 2x) dx + 2y e^x dy = 0
6. Check new exactness: M_y = 2y e^x, N_x = 2y e^x (EXACT!)
7. Integrate Exact Equation:
∫ [y const] (x² e^x + 2x e^x + y² e^x) dx = (x² e^x) + y² e^x
(No pure-y terms in N = 2ye^x to integrate)
SOLUTION: e^x (x² + y²) = C
DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS MATHEMATICAL BLUEPRINT // SCALE: 1.0 NATIVE // GATE / ESE / ISRO EXCELLENCE SUITE
